evidence: model_health_failure_classes_* (7 tests, crates/susi-gawd-swarm/src/tests/vc_202_020_mastery.rs — typed ModelHealth on the dispatch path); model_rate_arbitration_* (7 tests, crates/susi-gemi/src/tests/vc_202_020_rate_mastery.rs — per-key concurrency bound, per-key rate window + rollover, global bound across keys, shared process arbiter, production-cascade and probe-helper admission scans); availability_not_capability_* (5 tests, crates/susi-gemi/src/tests/availability_not_capability.rs — 40-failure transport storm leaves the ranking byte-identical while the health axis records it; wrong answers still move the ranking; dispatch-path scan)
notes: Health axis (T-DEEPSEEK-115): LockoutTracker::health reports every dispatch scope as a typed susi_core::model_health::ModelHealth — Healthy/Unhealthy{RateLimited} honouring Retry-After/Degraded/Unhealthy{ServiceError}/Dead{InvalidCredential|Unsupported|InsufficientQuota} — and run_jobs surfaces JobOutcome::target_health on the production dispatch path; capability ranking is structurally unaffected by availability storms (refutation-tested). Arbitration axis (T-DEEPSEEK-116): crates/susi-gemi/src/key_arbitration.rs is a process-global KeyArbiter enforcing per-key concurrency (default 4), a sliding per-key request-rate window (default 60/min), and a global in-flight ceiling (default 32), overridable via SUSI_KEY_ARBITRATION_*. Every production provider.generate call in susi-gemi admits through it: the failover cascade try_providers (engines/runtime.rs) skips a saturated key and tries the next provider, and all four one-shot probe helpers (coding_models_ext, frontier_ext, open_weight_ext, openrouter_ext) refuse on denial. Scope = registered provider name, which carries exactly one credential — the key pool. Honest limits: arbitration is process-global inside the daemon (external agent CLI subprocesses arbitrate in their own process; provider-side limits remain the backstop); the legacy susi-gawd model_rate_arbitration and susi-gawd-swarm parallel_admission/Shared::with_admission remain test-only machinery on the unreached swarm parallel-dispatch stack; susi-gawd-swarm cloud_recovery's direct provider.generate is not production-reached so it bypasses nothing in practice. Dispatch-axis fix (T-DEEPSEEK-117): the susi-gemi production cascade (engines/runtime.rs try_providers) previously folded every provider outcome into brain::record_outcome, so transport errors, rate limits, auth and funds failures all counted as capability failures. Now only actual model answers record capability evidence (Ok non-empty = success, Ok empty = failure), while Err stays on the health/cooldown axis via record_failure -> note_failure -> FailureKind. Refutation-tested: a 40-failure transport storm leaves success_rate/samples/rank byte-identical while last_failure shows (Transport, 40); a wrong answer still counts against capability.
